prompts.label: WHAT IS EC2 IMAGE BUILDER?
prompts.placeholder: EC2 Image Builder automates building, testing, and distributing machine images such as AMIs and supported…

reveal.text: EC2 Image Builder automates building, testing, and distributing machine images such as AMIs and supported container images.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it when hardened or standardized images should be produced repeatably instead of being manually…

reveal.text: Use it when hardened or standardized images should be produced repeatably instead of being manually configured.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A company releases a hardened AMI every month.

reveal.text: A company releases a hardened AMI every month. Image Builder starts from an approved base image, installs patches/security agents, runs tests, then distributes the approved AMI to target Regions/accounts.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Base image -> recipe/components -> build -> test -> distribute points to EC2 Image Builder.

reveal.text: Base image -> recipe/components -> build -> test -> distribute points to EC2 Image Builder.

prompts.label: HOW IT FLOWS
prompts.placeholder: Flow: Choose base image → … → Distribute approved image

prompts.label: WHAT IS AMAZON ECR?
prompts.placeholder: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) is a managed registry for storing and distributing container images.

reveal.text: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) is a managed registry for storing and distributing container images.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it when ECS, EKS, or other container runtimes need a private or public AWS-managed…

reveal.text: Use it when ECS, EKS, or other container runtimes need a private or public AWS-managed image registry.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A CI pipeline builds `checkout:2026-09-21`, pushes the image to ECR, and an ECS service pulls that exact image digest for deployment.

reveal.text: A CI pipeline builds `checkout:2026-09-21`, pushes the image to ECR, and an ECS service pulls that exact image digest for deployment. ECR stores the image; ECS/EKS runs it.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Container image repository/registry -> ECR.

reveal.text: Container image repository/registry -> ECR.

prompts.label: CONTAINER IMAGE DEPLOYMENT FLOW
prompts.placeholder: Build image → push to ECR → ECS/EKS pulls the image to run containers; registry success does not prove the runtime can pull it.

reveal.text: Amazon ECR stores container images. ECS or EKS then needs network reachability and IAM permissions to pull the image. In a troubleshooting scenario, separate an image-build/push problem from a runtime pull/launch problem.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS CLOUDFORMATION?
prompts.placeholder: AWS CloudFormation is AWS's declarative infrastructure-as-code service. A template describes resources and a stack is…

reveal.text: AWS CloudFormation is AWS's declarative infrastructure-as-code service. A template describes resources and a stack is the deployed instance of that template.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use CloudFormation when infrastructure should be repeatable, reviewable, and managed as a stack rather than…

reveal.text: Use CloudFormation when infrastructure should be repeatable, reviewable, and managed as a stack rather than through manual console changes.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A template declares an S3 bucket and IAM role.

reveal.text: A template declares an S3 bucket and IAM role. Deploying it creates a stack. Before an update that might replace a resource, a change set shows the proposed changes so the operator can review them first.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Template + stack + managed resource lifecycle -> CloudFormation.

reveal.text: Template + stack + managed resource lifecycle -> CloudFormation.

prompts.placeholder: Compare: Template • Stack • Change set • Drift detection

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS CDK?
prompts.placeholder: The AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK) lets you define AWS infrastructure with supported programming languages…

reveal.text: The AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK) lets you define AWS infrastructure with supported programming languages and synthesizes the result into CloudFormation templates.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use CDK when teams want higher-level constructs and familiar programming languages while retaining CloudFormation as…

reveal.text: Use CDK when teams want higher-level constructs and familiar programming languages while retaining CloudFormation as the deployment engine.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A TypeScript CDK app defines an S3 `Bucket` construct.

reveal.text: A TypeScript CDK app defines an S3 `Bucket` construct. Running `cdk synth` produces CloudFormation. CDK improves authoring ergonomics, but CloudFormation remains the deployment engine.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: CloudFormation • AWS CDK • Terraform

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Constructs -> synth -> CloudFormation stack points to CDK.

reveal.text: Constructs -> synth -> CloudFormation stack points to CDK.

prompts.label: WHAT IS CHANGE SETS VS DRIFT DETECTION?
prompts.placeholder: A CloudFormation change set previews proposed stack changes before execution. Drift detection compares supported actual…

reveal.text: A CloudFormation change set previews proposed stack changes before execution. Drift detection compares supported actual resource configuration with the expected stack configuration.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use change sets before applying a planned update; use drift detection when you suspect out-of-band…

reveal.text: Use change sets before applying a planned update; use drift detection when you suspect out-of-band changes.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A developer edits a security group manually in the console.

reveal.text: A developer edits a security group manually in the console. Drift detection can show that the actual resource no longer matches the CloudFormation-managed configuration. A change set instead previews a future stack update.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Change set • Drift detection

cells.what: Has a managed resource changed outside CloudFormation?

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Preview -> change set. Console edit outside CloudFormation -> drift.

reveal.text: Preview -> change set. Console edit outside CloudFormation -> drift.

prompts.label: HOW IT FLOWS
prompts.placeholder: Flow: Change IaC source → … → Later use drift detection for out-of-band changes

items: Later use drift detection for out-of-band changes

prompts.label: WHAT IS NESTED STACKS?
prompts.placeholder: A nested stack is a CloudFormation stack created as a resource inside another stack, allowing…

reveal.text: A nested stack is a CloudFormation stack created as a resource inside another stack, allowing reusable infrastructure components.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use nested stacks to break large templates into reusable managed pieces while keeping a parent-child…

reveal.text: Use nested stacks to break large templates into reusable managed pieces while keeping a parent-child stack relationship.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A company has one reusable CloudFormation template for its logging bucket and policies.

reveal.text: A company has one reusable CloudFormation template for its logging bucket and policies. Multiple parent stacks include it as a nested stack instead of copying the same resources into every template.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Reusable CloudFormation component embedded in a parent stack -> nested stack.

reveal.text: Reusable CloudFormation component embedded in a parent stack -> nested stack.

prompts.label: WHAT IS CLOUDFORMATION STACKSETS?
prompts.placeholder: CloudFormation StackSets deploy a common CloudFormation stack configuration to multiple AWS accounts and Regions.

reveal.text: CloudFormation StackSets deploy a common CloudFormation stack configuration to multiple AWS accounts and Regions.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use StackSets for centrally governed multi-account/multi-Region deployments; service-managed StackSets can integrate with AWS Organizations.

reveal.text: Use StackSets for centrally governed multi-account/multi-Region deployments; service-managed StackSets can integrate with AWS Organizations.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Security requires the same IAM role and Config rule in 40 accounts across two Regions.

reveal.text: Security requires the same IAM role and Config rule in 40 accounts across two Regions. StackSets can deploy the same stack configuration across those accounts/Regions from a central operation.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Same stack across many accounts/OUs and Regions -> StackSets.

reveal.text: Same stack across many accounts/OUs and Regions -> StackSets.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS RESOURCE ACCESS MANAGER?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) shares supported AWS resources with other accounts, organizational units…

reveal.text: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) shares supported AWS resources with other accounts, organizational units, or principals without duplicating the resource.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use RAM when supported resources should be centrally owned but shared across accounts.

reveal.text: Use RAM when supported resources should be centrally owned but shared across accounts.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A networking account owns a Transit Gateway that several application accounts should use.

reveal.text: A networking account owns a Transit Gateway that several application accounts should use. AWS RAM can share the supported resource instead of creating a separate Transit Gateway in every account.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: AWS RAM • StackSets

cells.use: Repeat the same infrastructure configuration across accounts/Regions

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Share one centrally owned supported resource rather than deploy one per account -> AWS RAM.

reveal.text: Share one centrally owned supported resource rather than deploy one per account -> AWS RAM.

prompts.label: WHAT IS CLOUDFORMATION DELETION AND RETENTION?
prompts.placeholder: CloudFormation deletion policies and related replacement/update policies control what happens to stateful resources or snapshots…

reveal.text: CloudFormation deletion policies and related replacement/update policies control what happens to stateful resources or snapshots when stacks or resources are removed or replaced.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use Retain or Snapshot-style policies where supported when stack deletion must not destroy important data.

reveal.text: Use Retain or Snapshot-style policies where supported when stack deletion must not destroy important data.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A CloudFormation stack contains an RDS database.

reveal.text: A CloudFormation stack contains an RDS database. The stack is deleted, but the database data must survive. A suitable deletion/retention policy can retain or snapshot the stateful resource instead of deleting it with the stack.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Delete the stack but keep the database/data -> inspect DeletionPolicy/retention behavior.

reveal.text: Delete the stack but keep the database/data -> inspect DeletionPolicy/retention behavior.

prompts.label: WHAT IS DEPLOYMENT TROUBLESHOOTING AND SUBNET CAPACITY?
prompts.placeholder: Deployment troubleshooting starts with the first failed resource and its error, then checks permissions, service…

reveal.text: Deployment troubleshooting starts with the first failed resource and its error, then checks permissions, service limits, dependencies, and network/subnet capacity.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: A subnet must have enough usable IP addresses for the resources being launched. IAM permissions…

reveal.text: A subnet must have enough usable IP addresses for the resources being launched. IAM permissions can also block resource creation even when the template is syntactically valid.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A stack fails while creating ENIs in a subnet with only 3 usable IP addresses remaining.

reveal.text: A stack fails while creating ENIs in a subnet with only 3 usable IP addresses remaining. The template syntax is valid; the real problem is subnet capacity. Stack events show the first failed resource and reason.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: CloudFormation stack events identify the first failed resource; subnet IP exhaustion can prevent EC2/ENI launches.

reveal.text: CloudFormation stack events identify the first failed resource; subnet IP exhaustion can prevent EC2/ENI launches.

prompts.label: DEPLOYMENT PERMISSION TRAP: IAM:PASSROLE
prompts.placeholder: A deployment can create a service resource but still fail when assigning its execution role if the caller lacks iam:PassRole.

reveal.text: A deployment can fail when an AWS service needs to use an IAM role but the caller lacks `iam:PassRole`. This permission lets the caller pass the role to the service. It does not let the caller assume the role. Separate this from missing permissions inside the role itself.

prompts.label: WHAT IS GIT AND IAC WORKFLOW?
prompts.placeholder: Git version control records infrastructure-code history and enables review, branching, collaboration, and rollback context.

reveal.text: Git version control records infrastructure-code history and enables review, branching, collaboration, and rollback context.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use version control and review as the source of intended infrastructure changes instead of undocumented…

reveal.text: Use version control and review as the source of intended infrastructure changes instead of undocumented console edits.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: An engineer changes a Terraform security-group rule in a branch, opens a pull request, and the plan is reviewed before merge.

reveal.text: An engineer changes a Terraform security-group rule in a branch, opens a pull request, and the plan is reviewed before merge. Git provides the history/review trail; the IaC tool performs the infrastructure change.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Need an auditable review history for Terraform/CloudFormation code -> Git/version control.

reveal.text: Need an auditable review history for Terraform/CloudFormation code -> Git/version control.

prompts.label: WHAT IS TERRAFORM?
prompts.placeholder: Terraform is a third-party infrastructure-as-code tool. It uses configuration, providers, and state to plan and…

reveal.text: Terraform is a third-party infrastructure-as-code tool. It uses configuration, providers, and state to plan and apply changes to managed resources.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use Terraform when its provider ecosystem and workflow fit the organization; protect remote state and…

reveal.text: Use Terraform when its provider ecosystem and workflow fit the organization; protect remote state and review plans before apply.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Terraform configuration declares an `aws_s3_bucket`.

reveal.text: Terraform configuration declares an `aws_s3_bucket`. `terraform plan` proposes the change based on config/state/remote objects; `terraform apply` executes the approved plan. State is not the desired configuration itself.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Configuration • State • Plan • Apply

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Provider + state + plan/apply -> Terraform.

reveal.text: Provider + state + plan/apply -> Terraform.

prompts.placeholder: Key lines: Required provider • Provider configuration • Managed resource

annotations.title: Provider configuration
annotations.explanation: The provider configures access/behavior for AWS.

prompts.label: WHAT IS DEPLOYMENT STRATEGIES?
prompts.placeholder: A deployment strategy controls how new application or infrastructure versions replace old ones and how…

reveal.text: A deployment strategy controls how new application or infrastructure versions replace old ones and how much old/new capacity runs at the same time.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose in-place/rolling for lower duplicate-capacity cost, blue/green for isolated old/new environments and fast rollback, and…

reveal.text: Choose in-place/rolling for lower duplicate-capacity cost, blue/green for isolated old/new environments and fast rollback, and canary for gradual exposure where supported.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Version 2 of an API is deployed to a separate green environment while version 1 remains blue.

reveal.text: Version 2 of an API is deployed to a separate green environment while version 1 remains blue. After validation, traffic switches to green. If errors rise, traffic can move back quickly to blue.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Rolling/in-place • Blue/green • Canary

cells.use: Less duplicate capacity, rollback may be slower

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Fast rollback with separate old/new environments -> blue/green.

reveal.text: Fast rollback with separate old/new environments -> blue/green.

prompts.label: CONTROLLED SELF-SERVICE PROVISIONING
prompts.placeholder: Need users to launch only approved infrastructure products with governed options/tags? AWS Service Catalog is designed for controlled self-service provisioning.

reveal.text: AWS Service Catalog lets administrators create portfolios of approved products that users can provision through controlled interfaces. For supported product types, TagOptions provide managed key/value choices that help keep provisioned-product tags consistent. AWS Service Catalog does not support TagOptions for Terraform Open Source or Terraform Cloud products.

prompts.label: WHAT IS SYSTEMS MANAGER OPERATIONS?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Systems Manager is a collection of operational capabilities for managing nodes and AWS resources…

reveal.text: AWS Systems Manager is a collection of operational capabilities for managing nodes and AWS resources, including commands, patching, sessions, desired state, automation, and maintenance scheduling.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose the specific Systems Manager capability that matches the job instead of treating Systems Manager…

reveal.text: Choose the specific Systems Manager capability that matches the job instead of treating Systems Manager as one generic tool.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A fleet needs patching, recurring agent enforcement, occasional shell access, and multi-step remediation.

reveal.text: A fleet needs patching, recurring agent enforcement, occasional shell access, and multi-step remediation. Patch Manager, State Manager, Session Manager, and Automation each solve a different part of that operations workload.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: The exam often tests which Systems Manager feature fits the operational task.

reveal.text: The exam often tests which Systems Manager feature fits the operational task.

prompts.label: SYSTEMS MANAGER TOOL CHOICES
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Run Command • Automation • State Manager • Patch Manager

prompts.label: WHAT IS RUN COMMAND?
prompts.placeholder: Run Command executes commands or Systems Manager documents on managed nodes without opening inbound administrative…

reveal.text: Run Command executes commands or Systems Manager documents on managed nodes without opening inbound administrative ports.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it for direct fleet commands, scripts, or one-time operational tasks.

reveal.text: Use it for direct fleet commands, scripts, or one-time operational tasks.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Run Command targets 200 managed nodes tagged `App=web` and executes `sudo systemctl reload nginx`.

reveal.text: Run Command targets 200 managed nodes tagged `App=web` and executes `sudo systemctl reload nginx`. The operator does not need to open SSH or log into each instance.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Run a command on tagged managed instances -> Run Command.

reveal.text: Run a command on tagged managed instances -> Run Command.

prompts.placeholder: Key lines: Command document • Targets • Command

annotations.explanation: Run Command uses a Systems Manager document that defines the command behavior.

prompts.label: WHAT IS PATCH MANAGER VS STATE MANAGER?
prompts.placeholder: Patch Manager assesses and installs operating-system patches. State Manager creates associations that apply or verify…

reveal.text: Patch Manager assesses and installs operating-system patches. State Manager creates associations that apply or verify desired configuration on managed nodes.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use Patch Manager for patch compliance/install; use State Manager when a configuration or agent should…

reveal.text: Use Patch Manager for patch compliance/install; use State Manager when a configuration or agent should remain in a desired state.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Patch Manager installs approved OS patches during maintenance.

reveal.text: Patch Manager installs approved OS patches during maintenance. State Manager separately ensures the CloudWatch agent remains installed/configured every day. Patching and desired configuration are related but different jobs.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Patch Manager • State Manager

cells.use: Keep software/configuration in the expected state

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Ensure an agent remains installed -> State Manager; install approved OS patches -> Patch Manager.

reveal.text: Ensure an agent remains installed -> State Manager; install approved OS patches -> Patch Manager.

prompts.label: WHAT IS MAINTENANCE WINDOWS VS SESSION MANAGER?
prompts.placeholder: Maintenance Windows schedule recurring operational tasks against targets. Session Manager provides controlled interactive access to…

reveal.text: Maintenance Windows schedule recurring operational tasks against targets. Session Manager provides controlled interactive access to managed nodes without inbound SSH/RDP.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use Maintenance Windows for approved scheduled work; use Session Manager when an operator needs an…

reveal.text: Use Maintenance Windows for approved scheduled work; use Session Manager when an operator needs an interactive shell/session.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Production patching is approved Sundays 02:00-04:00, so a Maintenance Window defines when tasks may run.

reveal.text: Production patching is approved Sundays 02:00-04:00, so a Maintenance Window defines when tasks may run. An engineer troubleshooting one host interactively uses Session Manager instead.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Schedule patching every Sunday -> Maintenance Window. Interactive shell without SSH -> Session Manager.

reveal.text: Schedule patching every Sunday -> Maintenance Window. Interactive shell without SSH -> Session Manager.

prompts.label: WHAT IS SYSTEMS MANAGER AUTOMATION?
prompts.placeholder: Systems Manager Automation executes multi-step runbooks that can call AWS APIs, run scripts, branch, wait…

reveal.text: Systems Manager Automation executes multi-step runbooks that can call AWS APIs, run scripts, branch, wait, and invoke other automation.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it for repeatable operational workflows that are more complex than one direct command.

reveal.text: Use it for repeatable operational workflows that are more complex than one direct command.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A remediation runbook stops an instance, snapshots its volume, changes a tag, waits for the snapshot, and starts the instance again.

reveal.text: A remediation runbook stops an instance, snapshots its volume, changes a tag, waits for the snapshot, and starts the instance again. Automation coordinates the steps instead of requiring five manual console actions.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Multi-step remediation/runbook -> Automation.

reveal.text: Multi-step remediation/runbook -> Automation.

prompts.label: WHAT IS EVENTBRIDGE AUTOMATION?
prompts.placeholder: EventBridge routes matching events to configured targets using rules on event buses.

reveal.text: EventBridge routes matching events to configured targets using rules on event buses.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it when a state change or application event should trigger automation without polling.

reveal.text: Use it when a state change or application event should trigger automation without polling.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A CloudFormation stack enters `ROLLBACK_COMPLETE`.

reveal.text: A CloudFormation stack enters `ROLLBACK_COMPLETE`. EventBridge matches the state-change event and invokes a Step Functions workflow that gathers evidence and opens an operations ticket.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Match event pattern -> invoke target -> EventBridge.

reveal.text: Match event pattern -> invoke target -> EventBridge.

prompts.placeholder: Flow: Event occurs → … → Verify result

prompts.label: WHAT IS LAMBDA AUTOMATION?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Lambda runs code in response to events without managing servers.

reveal.text: AWS Lambda runs code in response to events without managing servers.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it for short custom automation and API orchestration triggered by EventBridge, S3, or other…

reveal.text: Use it for short custom automation and API orchestration triggered by EventBridge, S3, or other event sources.

reveal.text: Small custom event-driven function -> Lambda.

reveal.text: S3 Event Notifications publish notifications when configured object events occur in a bucket.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS DEVOPS AGENT?
prompts.placeholder: AWS DevOps Agent is an AI-powered service that spans release management and production operations, including…

reveal.text: AWS DevOps Agent is an AI-powered service that spans release management and production operations, including investigating operational issues and identifying improvements.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: For SOA-C03, know the role at a high level: AI-assisted operational investigation and automation context…

reveal.text: For SOA-C03, know the role at a high level: AI-assisted operational investigation and automation context, not product-internal details.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: After a deployment, 5XX errors increase.

reveal.text: After a deployment, 5XX errors increase. AWS DevOps Agent can assist with production-operations investigation using connected operational context. The point is incident/release operations, not replacing IAM or CloudWatch fundamentals.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: The blueprint explicitly names AWS DevOps Agent for event-driven/operational automation.

reveal.text: The blueprint explicitly names AWS DevOps Agent for event-driven/operational automation.
